Subject: Prompt set collection & model-fit next steps — Acme

Hey Sam / Elena — great call today, thanks for walking through the search assistant use case and the sample queries. Quick recap + next steps so we’re aligned:

1) Goals we heard: improve recall on internal docs, reduce hallucinations for 'policy' queries, and surface authorized content only (redaction/PII concerns).
2) Data scope: 8k docs in knowledge base, mixed internal/external, ~30% semi-structured (PDFs, emails).
3) Success metrics: +10% top-1 accuracy on canonical queries, reduce high-confidence hallucinations by 50%.

Ask: can you share a representative prompt set (user queries + expected answer/acceptance criteria) and point out edge cases (PII, legal disclaimers, templates)? Attached is a prompt_set_template.csv to make collection easy. If you can redline where PII should be masked vs. retrievable, that’ll inform our redaction policy.

Model recommendations (shortlist for initial eval):
- redwood-alpha-7b-chat (fast, good for cheap baseline)
- llama-2-13b-chat (strong instruction-following, good for QA)
- mistral-instruct-8x (competitive on instruction tasks)
We’ll run these across your prompt set and compare latency/cost/accuracy.

Benchmarks and evaluation docs: https://drive.redwood.ai/benchmarks/acme-model-fit-2026 (private link)

Attachments: acme_prompt_set_template.csv, redaction_guidance_v1.pdf

Next steps:
- Sam: share initial prompt set + list of redaction rules by EOD Friday (Jul 2)
- Redwood: we'll kick off an initial model-fit eval and send a short summary + sample failures within 3 business days of receiving the prompts

Thanks — excited to move this forward.

--
Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — attached are two CSVs: our initial 40 user queries (varied intents) and a small set of expected extracts for 12 canonical queries. Quick notes / questions:

- We flagged several queries that include customer names and order numbers. Do you recommend we send those with tokens redacted (e.g., ORDER_####) or as-is with an allowlist?
- A few queries are very short / conversational; we flagged those as likely to need more context (session history).
- We’re worried about regression: we tuned an on-prem model last year and saw a drop in accuracy when we moved from 7B->13B because of different tokenization. How do you detect and prevent quality regressions across model/quantization variants?

Sam

--
Sam Torres
Product Manager, Search & Discovery

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Prompt set collection & model-fit follow-up — Acme

Great, Sam — got the files, thanks. Short answers:

- Redaction guidance: send the prompts with placeholder tokens for PII (ORDER_####, NAME_REDACTED) where possible. If you need highest-fidelity evaluation (to catch context-sensitive errors), send a separate secure file with real values and we’ll run it in Private mode with KMS protections.
- Short prompts: we’ll augment with 2-3 lines of synthetic session context when evaluating to approximate real sessions; results will include a note when session context materially changes output.
- Regression detection: we run prompt-level diffs across model variants and quantization profiles and flag "quality regressions" where the newer config drops below your acceptance criteria. We also keep deterministic seed snapshots for reruns. Rishi will include sample evaluation config (metrics + thresholds).

I’m looping in Rishi with the proposed evaluation config and our template for expected outputs. Rishi — can you attach the quick eval config and an example failure report (simple HTML) we’ll share with Acme?

Thanks — will start the model-fit runs as soon as we get the redacted + secure prompt sets.

--
Marissa

On Wed, Jul 1, 2026 at 12:18 PM Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai> wrote:
> I’m looping in Rishi with the proposed evaluation config and our template for expected outputs. Rishi — can you attach the quick eval config and an example failure report (simple HTML) we’ll share with Acme?

Attached: quick_eval_config.json (sample), example_failure_report.html (sample) — I’m sending as inline snippets here for convenience. Key pieces:

- Metrics: top-1 accuracy, token-level F1 for extractions, hallucination_rate (binary), latency_95th, cost_per_1k_tokens.
- Thresholds: top-1 >= 0.70 on canonical set, hallucination_rate <= 0.10.
- Process: run each model/quantization against full prompt set, compute diffs vs. baseline (your current on-prem baseline), and produce per-prompt regression flags.

Important redaction note for Acme: if you include PII placeholders in the main CSV and send the real-value CSV via our Private upload link, mark the rows with "PII=true" so the eval pipeline applies masked logging and KMS-wrapped storage.

Next steps for Redwood: we’ll kick off the runs and share an interim report with top 10 failure cases and recommended model/config for your use case. Expect that within 72 hours of the secure prompt set.

— Rishi
